question: What must a Speed Limit sign display, in what increments, and may it be used to show an advisory speed for a roadway condition?
model_answer: Direct Answer: A Speed Limit (R2-1) sign must display the limit established by law, ordinance, regulation, or as adopted by the authorized agency based on an engineering study, and the displayed limits must be in multiples of 5 mph. A Speed Limit sign should not be used to show an advisory speed for a roadway condition; instead, an Advisory Speed plaque mounted below a warning sign is the recommended (and, in specific cases, optional) tool for advisory speeds. Standards (mandatory): - "The Speed Limit (R2-1) sign (see Figure 2B-3) shall display the limit established by law, ordinance, regulation, or as adopted by the authorized agency based on an engineering study. The speed limits displayed shall be in multiples of 5 mph." - For variable speed limit signs on freeways and expressways: "The regulatory speed displayed on a variable Speed Limit sign shall comply with Paragraph 13" of Section 2B.21. Guidance (recommended): - Per the guidance visible on the page containing Section 2B.21: an advisory speed plaque (see Section 2C.59) mounted below a warning sign should be used to warn road users of an advisory speed for a roadway condition; a Speed Limit sign should not be used for this purpose. Options (permitted): - "An Advisory Speed plaque (see Figure 2C-1 and Section 2C.59) may be used when the change in roadway condition requires a reduced speed." - "An Advisory Exit Speed or Advisory Ramp Speed sign may be used based on engineering judgment when the difference between the mainline roadway speed limit and the exit or ramp advisory speed in the vicinity of the departure is 10 mph or less." - "A Speed Limit Sign Beacon may be used with a fixed or variable Speed Limit sign," and a flashing Speed Limit Sign Beacon (with an appropriate accompanying sign) may be used to indicate that the displayed speed limit is in effect. Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 2B-3 illustrates the R2-1 Speed Limit sign ("SPEED LIMIT 50") and related speed limit signs and plaques, all showing speeds in multiples of 5 mph (50, 40, 45, 55, 30). - [Image 2] Shows Figure 2C-2, where advisory speeds for a horizontal curve are conveyed by W13-1P Advisory Speed plaques ("35 MPH") mounted below curve warning signs — not by Speed Limit signs. - [Image 3] Shows the full text of Section 2B.21, including Standard §13 (limit established by law/engineering study, multiples of 5 mph) and the guidance that a Speed Limit sign should not be used to warn of an advisory speed for a roadway condition. - [Image 4] Full-page view of Figure 2B-3 confirming the layout and designations (R2-1 through R2-14) of Speed Limit signs and plaques. - [Image 5] Shows a Speed Limit 35 sign with red/orange flags as an example of enhanced conspicuity, consistent with the R2-1 sign displaying a regulatory limit in a multiple of 5 mph. Citations: - Section 2B.21 Standard §13 (p.85) - Section 2G.26 Standard §3 (p.457) - Section 2C.28 Option §2 (p.173) - Section 2C.12 Option §5 (p.160) - Section 4S.04 Option §3 (p.753) - Figure 2B-3 (p.86) - Page 126
gold_answer: It must display the speed limit established by law, ordinance, regulation, or an authorized agency based on an engineering study, in multiples of 5 mph. It should not be used for an advisory speed; an advisory speed plaque below an appropriate warning sign should be used instead.
